analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md: the date is bumped, and the GLM video paragraph (base lines ~810-811, 827) now says variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime video is indexed at i / nominalFrameRate instead of being refused with a deterministic 400. The patch excerpt is truncated; the head ranges 876-895 and 1732-1751 are not visible in the supplied units, so those additions were not reviewed. The two supplied units show only the base text (lines 416-1208).

Possible security relevance, which is code behavior I cannot see rather than anything in the docs: if the processor code (GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset) really stopped refusing VFR video, the new path must still honor the decoded-frame cap (512 MiB maximumDecodedBytes), the 28,532 visual-token cap, and the VisionMemoryGate reservation. A VFR track could have a very high frame count, so decoding is bounded by cap enforcement rather than by the old refusal. This is a DoS/availability concern (T-010/TB-007 class) for media inputs from a consumer through the coordinator. The docs say frames are read in presentation order and only the 2 FPS sample is kept within the cap, which suggests bounds are maintained, but the implementation diff is not in this batch.

No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by the docs text. The prefix-cache (T-041), the SSD tier, the media exclusion from prefix lookup, and the cache scope claims are unchanged in the visible text. Remaining integration question: confirm in the source diff that the VFR frame indexing path enforces the frame and byte caps before allocation, and that timestamp text derived from nominalFrameRate cannot divide by zero or overflow when the rate is 0 or NaN.
